findings.claim: Row r4 requires a Hermes viking_search that returns memories, and its evidence is not recorded. The briefing lists it under Not observed. The row's fails_when counts missing evidence as a failure. The Hermes job running now (0.22.2, upstream plugin) already calls this OpenViking, so the check can be made without the unlanded hermes ticket.

Comments and a proposal page still name the old versions. services.tf:468 says `:latest` and v0.4.17.1 resolve to one digest today. .okf/proposals/openviking-dashboard.md:47-49 says that at HEAD the Dockerfile pins ov-postgres-v0.6.0 and ov-ext-v0.7.1 and the base is still 0.4.17.1. The justfile verify recipe still echoes "checking the ov-retrieval entry point". Inside the jobspec, openviking.hcl:90-92 quotes a /health measured on v0.4.17.1-9 and says "Re-measure when the image moves", and the comment above OV_RETRIEVAL_RERANK_POOLING still says "Cap the number of calls", which described the MAX_CALLS setting this change removed.

entries.change: No code change: the missing evidence is now in. On 2026-11-27, after OpenViking v0.5.6-1 went live, the operator ran a memory search through Hermes over Telegram and it returned memories, so Hermes's viking_search works against 0.5.6 through the running Hermes job and its plugin.

The ### comment above nomad_job.openviking no longer claims :latest and v0.4.17.1 share a digest; it says :latest moves with every release. Outside the jobspec, so the plan shows no change to the job.
The provenance note names the current pins, ov-postgres-v0.7.0 and ov-ext-v0.8.0, on base 0.5.6.

The verify recipe now prints 'checking the ov_ext entry point'. The two stale comments inside openviking.hcl (the v0.4.17.1 /health quote and the rerank-cap comment) are left as they are on purpose: editing a jobspec comment re-registers the job, which .claude/rules/terraform-file-layout.md says is not worth it for a comment.
